$comment: D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE: a `wmain`-only program targeting ELF has NO program entry and is REFUSED. THIS PINS A MEASURED THREE-PART DEFECT: on HEAD 3e86a187 (2026-08-10, build-dbg) this source was refused by a message that (i) asserted `wmain` WAS the Linux program entry -- candidate selection matched entry NAMES alone and was format-blind; (ii) prescribed adding an ELF config row, a remedy that would have MADE it the Linux entry and shipped a binary whose entry expects a wide argument vector no Linux loader produces; and (iii) cited an unrelated anchor about main's envp parameter. A message confidently wrong in three ways is worse than a vague one, because the reader follows it. * THE NEAR-MISS CLAUSE IS LOAD-BEARING: the diagnostic now names both the fact (no entry this format can start) and the reason (`wmain` is defined but needs the `argc-wargv` verb this format does not realize). Without the reason the reader is told an entry is missing while looking straight at what appears to be one. * gcc's answer to the same source is `undefined reference to 'main'` -- the same fact, later and with no reason. The link tier's existence checks are NOT superseded; they still cover an entry from an object DSS never compiled, where no signature is in the input. * `positioned: false` is honest: this is a WHOLE-PROGRAM fact with no single declaration at fault. * RED-ON-DISABLE: add "argc-wargv" to the ELF exec format's `entryVerbs` and this stops erroring -- `wmain` would be selected as the ELF entry, which is the defect itself.
